title: The Myth of Eurasia
gist: This review essay (cut off by a paywall after its opening) argues that Vladimir Putin frames the war in Ukraine as a civilizational struggle rooted in Russia's claimed Eurasian imperial identity, citing his October 2022 Valdai Club speech on 'civilizational diversity' as evidence.

themes.theme: Putin's civilizational framing of the Ukraine war

insights.claim: Putin has cast the invasion of Ukraine as part of a broader civilizational struggle rather than solely a territorial or security conflict, a framing that some of his Western adversaries have implicitly accepted as well.
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Suggests the war's ideological framing (civilizational rather than purely strategic) could make negotiated settlement harder, since civilizational claims are less amenable to conventional territorial or security-guarantee bargaining.
insights.quote: From the outset, Russian President Vladimir Putin has cast his invasion as part of a cultural struggle, a view shared by some of his adversaries on the Western side.

insights.claim: In October 2022, while grappling with the disappointing course of the war he had begun months earlier, Putin used a speech at the Valdai International Discussion Club to advocate for 'civilizational diversity.'
insights.speaker: Foreign Affairs
insights.so_what: Marks a specific dated instance where Putin pivoted to civilizational rhetoric under battlefield pressure, useful as a reference point for tracking how Kremlin messaging shifts with war fortunes.
insights.quote: In October 2022, as he grappled with the disappointing course of the war he had begun just months earlier, he used a speech at the Valdai International Discussion Club to advocate “civilizational diversity.”
